t: #3588 Find Maximum Area of a Triangle — Axis-Parallel Side
o: Among all triangles formed by three input points having at least one side parallel to an axis, maximize twice the area. Twice the area of a triangle with horizontal base (x1,y)-(x2,y) and apex (x3,y3) is |x1-x2| * |y3-y|. Example 1: base (1,2)-(3,2), apex (1,1) → 2*1*1 = 2. Example 2: collinear diagonal points admit no axis-parallel side → -1. n up to 1e5 forbids O(n³).
k: Fix the axis-parallel side: for a horizontal side at height y, the best width in that row is max_x - min_x, and the best apex height is the global farthest y different from this row.
Symmetrically handle vertical sides by swapping roles of x and y.
Global min/max coordinates suffice for the apex — no per-point search needed.

a.i: Try all O(n³) triples, check the axis-parallel condition, compute twice the cross-product area. Only viable conceptually — too slow for n = 1e5 but useful for validating the fast solution.
s: If any two share x or y, compute |cross product| / 1 (twice area via determinant).
a.t: O(n³) — only feasible for tiny inputs.

a.n: Approach 2: Group by Row/Column with Global Extremes (Optimal)
a.i: Group points by y (rows). A horizontal-base triangle uses two points in one row — the widest pair is (min x, max x) of that row — plus an apex anywhere else; the tallest apex is whichever of the global min-y / max-y differs from the row. Do the mirror-image for columns. This covers every optimal triangle because widening the base or raising the apex never hurts.
s: Bucket x-coordinates by y and y-coordinates by x; compute global min/max of each axis.
For each row with ≥ 2 points: candidate = (max_x - min_x) * max(|y - ymin|, |y - ymax|), skipping zero height.
a.t: O(n) — one pass to bucket and find extremes, one pass over groups.

w: The greedy 'widest base in the row, farthest apex globally' exchange argument is the heart of the problem. Watch for: all points on one line (return -1), needing 64-bit products (coordinates up to 1e6 give values up to ~1e12), and remembering to handle both horizontal and vertical sides. Follow-up: maximize the actual area of any triangle without the axis-parallel restriction (rotating calipers / convex hull).
